claims.title: What does the rank of convolution say about the sum of its coefficients?
claims.hypotheses: H is a finite ℓ-group. The coefficients of the regular convolution matrix are bounded by one in an ultrametric field.
claims.statement: For N group elements and convolution rank r, the Nth power of the norm of the coefficient sum is bounded by |ℓ| to the power N−r.

claims.title: Which local operator fixes the forms that fail the test?
claims.hypotheses: The tested place is split, with hyperspecial level. The test polynomial is nonzero. A failed local system has an occurring smooth irreducible realization with a tuple on its zero set.
claims.statement: The spherical transform supplies a finite sum of translations acting by one on all failing fixed vectors, with arbitrarily small sum of squared complex coefficients. At a different underlying prime the translations are trivial.

claims.title: How does a cyclic character impose a local type?

claims.title: Why do the conjugate forms fit in one finite-dimensional space?
claims.hypotheses: A nonzero algebraic automorphic form on the definite unitary group has fixed finite level and a finite-dimensional span of archimedean translates. The selected Hecke operators are rational.
claims.statement: The conjugates prescribed on the finite adelic group extend to continuous automorphic forms of the same finite level and bounded archimedean polynomial degree. Evaluation on h class representatives embeds their common space into h copies of the polynomials of degree at most D in b coordinates.

claims.title: Why does each nontrivial character force cuspidality?
claims.hypotheses: The local group is GL of positive rank over a finite extension of the ℓ-adic field. An identity neighbourhood and a lower bound on the exponent are prescribed.
claims.statement: There is a torsion-free compact open subgroup in the neighbourhood with a surjection onto a cyclic quotient of the prescribed minimum order. Every smooth irreducible complex representation containing a nonzero vector of any nontrivial character pulled back from this quotient is cuspidal.
